title: ‘’Then they reached Jericho, and as Jesus and his disciples left town, a large crowd followed him. A blind beggar named Bartimaeus (son of Timaeus) was sitting beside the road.  When Bartimaeus heard that Jesus of Nazareth was nearby, he began to shout, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”  “Be quiet!” many of the people yelled at him. But he only shouted louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me. When Jesus heard him, he stopped and said, “Tell him to come here.” So they called the blind man. “Cheer up,” they said. “Come on, he’s calling you!”  Bartimaeus threw aside his coat, jumped up, and came to Jesus.  “What do you want me to do for you?” Jesus asked. “My rabbi,” the blind man said, “I want to see!”  And Jesus said to him, “Go, for your faith has healed you.” Instantly the man could see, and he followed Jesus down the road.’’
scripture_text: The Holler in the dark. The story of Bartimeus.
devotional:
Jesus is making his way to Jerusalem; He is going there to fulfil all the purposes of his father. This was the most important journey that was ever made by anyone in history. It was more important than Neil Armstrong’s journey to the moon, more important than Edmund Hillary’s journey to the top of Everest, more important than Columbus journey on the Santa Maria when he discovered America. It was even more important that the journey Princess Elizabeth made to Westminster Abbey to be crowned Queen. This journey was more important than any journey you or I will ever make. We have all made important journeys, some wonderful, some dark and sad. But nothing like this journey, for at the end of this journey history would be redefined, and the world would never be the same. Jesus was journeying to Jerusalem where he would die on a cross in order to free mankind from the power of sin and satan.

While on this journey Jesus did something that was amazing. He stopped. He put his journey on hold. He suspended the eternal purposes of God for a few seconds to respond to the holler in the dark. Jesus stopped to respond to the cries of a man called Blind Bartimeus.

Bartimeus was a very interesting and unique person. He is the only named person in the bible who Jesus healed physically. The reason why he is named is because his name tells us a lot about him. In the time of Jesus a person’s name was more than a title, it was more like a description of the person. Bartimeus means ‘son of Timaeus’ or ‘son of honour.’ We know nothing about his background, but with a name like Bartimeus it is safe to assume that he was not always a beggar that he had not always lived as an outcast. As a blind beggar he would have been filled with shame as he lived in his own dark world, a world that was so isolated, that those on their way to a religious feast in Jerusalem could not enter into or care about.

Try and imagine what life must had been like for Bartimeus, homeless and dark. Someone who was despised looked down upon, then Jesus comes into his life, and he experienced the power of grace and Devine acceptance.

We also know that Bartimeus was not always blind. When Bartimeaus said to Jesus, ‘Rabbi I want to see’ the word used means to see again. We don’t know why he went blind, but we do know that in culture and at that time blindness was understood as a form of punishment for some kind of wrong behaviour.

So out of the darkness comes this heart wrenching cry. ‘Son of David have mercy on me.’ The religious crowd tried to shut him up, tried to silence him, they wanted to ignore his plight and take away his voice. They wanted to control him by using harsh words, [ “Be quiet!” many of the people yelled at him.] The Greek word for yelled is epitimao which carries the idea, to find fault with, to censure severely, to rebuke, to express strong disapproval of, or to denounce.

Yet Jesus’ reaction was completely different, he stopped. The heart of Jesus is touched by this man’s desperate cry, so he stopped.

He stopped and invited the man into his space, into his world. He calls Bartimeus from his darkness and his shame. Jesus stopped in the middle of this epic journey to ask this lonely, shameful beggar ‘What can I do for you?’

He stopped to listen, to listen to Bartimeus’ cry, his heart, his longing, his request. He creates time to listen. In the middle of noise, activity, mayhem and the crowds, Jesus stopped to engage, encourage and enrich the life of a humiliated beggar.

Mark tells us that Bartimaeus threw aside his coat, jumped up, and came to Jesus. Mark 10:50. This cloak was an item of clothing, that defined that he was a beggar. It was like his permission slip or a licence to be sitting there begging for money. If you were wearing a cloak like that it showed the people around you that you were a beggar. It was his identity. In bible times, being blind was often seen as a curse. There was really no way to support yourself financially, so beggars were given cloaks, which gave them permission to beg. They would have been defined as such by the cloak they wore. Usually, their cloak was the beggar’s one and only possession and their only source of income. Notice that Bartimeus threw away his cloak before he was healed. This showed Jesus that he had faith in Him to heal him. He threw away his cloak recognising that he was no longer a beggar but a son of God. His identity was totally changed.

Often as Christians we say to God, ‘If you do this for me I will….’ Sometimes we need to throw away the ‘symbols’ ‘cloaks’ of our past so we can freely follow Jesus.

Jesus is never blinded to the needs of others by his pressing responsibilities or chaotic activity that may be going on around him, Jesus will always find time to stop.
prayer: Father thank you for this amazing story about Jesus who stopped on his way to the cross for a blind beggar.
